title: Magnets
description: Magnets attract iron and steel objects. Every magnet has two poles: North (N) and South (S). Opposite poles attract; same poles repel.

exercises.question: Which object will a magnet ATTRACT?
exercises.exp: Paper clips are made of steel — magnets attract iron and steel objects!

exercises.question: What are the two poles of a magnet called?
exercises.exp: Every magnet has a North pole and a South pole.

exercises.question: Two magnets with the SAME poles facing each other will ___.
exercises.exp: Like poles (N-N or S-S) repel — they push each other away!

exercises.question: North pole of one magnet is held near the SOUTH pole of another. They will ___.
exercises.exp: Opposite poles attract — North and South pull toward each other!

exercises.question: Can a magnet attract a copper coin?
choices: only if the coin is cold
exercises.exp: Copper is not magnetic. Magnets attract iron, steel, nickel, and cobalt.

exercises.question: Which objects would a magnet attract? Choose the best answer.
choices: iron nails, steel scissors, a nickel coin
exercises.exp: Iron, steel, and nickel are magnetic metals. The others are not.

exercises.question: Static electricity is similar to magnets because it ___.
exercises.exp: Like magnets, static electricity can attract (and sometimes repel) objects.

exercises.question: A magnet can attract a paper clip THROUGH a piece of paper. This shows magnets ___.
exercises.exp: Magnetic force can pass through non-magnetic materials like paper, plastic, and water.

exercises.question: Which everyday item uses magnets?
exercises.exp: Refrigerator doors use magnets in the seal to keep the door closed tightly!

exercises.question: What shape do most bar magnets come in?
exercises.exp: A bar magnet is long and rectangular with N at one end and S at the other.

exercises.question: Where is the magnetic force of a bar magnet STRONGEST?
exercises.exp: The magnetic force is strongest at the two poles — the ends of the magnet.

exercises.question: A horseshoe magnet is shaped like a U. Where are its poles?
choices: at the curve of the U
at both open ends of the U
exercises.exp: The two open ends of a horseshoe magnet are its N and S poles — both face the same direction!

exercises.question: What happens to the magnetic force when you move a magnet FARTHER from an object?
exercises.exp: Magnetic force weakens with distance — the farther away, the weaker the pull or push.

exercises.question: Can a magnet attract a STEEL nail? Why?
choices: yes, steel contains iron and iron is attracted to magnets
only if the nail is painted
exercises.exp: Steel is an alloy that contains iron — iron is magnetic, so steel nails are attracted to magnets!

exercises.question: You rub an iron nail with a magnet many times in one direction. What might happen?
choices: the nail becomes a temporary magnet itself
the nail loses all metal properties
exercises.exp: Stroking iron with a magnet aligns its tiny magnetic domains — making it a temporary magnet!

exercises.question: Which of these is NOT attracted to a magnet?
exercises.exp: Gold is not magnetic — it is a precious metal but magnets have no effect on it. Iron and steel ARE magnetic.

exercises.question: Two bar magnets are placed end to end: N-S | N-S (same arrangement). They will ___.
exercises.exp: The S pole of the left magnet faces the N pole of the right magnet — opposite poles attract!

exercises.question: A compass is a tool with a MAGNETIC NEEDLE. The needle always points ___.
choices: toward geographic North (Earth's magnetic north pole)
exercises.exp: Earth is a giant magnet! A compass needle aligns with Earth's magnetic field and always points North.

exercises.question: Which of these would a magnet NOT attract?
exercises.exp: Wood is not magnetic. Iron filings, steel scissors, and nickel coins are all attracted to magnets!

exercises.question: A magnet can pick up paper clips from the BOTTOM of a glass of water. This shows ___.
choices: magnetic force passes through water (a non-magnetic material)
paper clips are attracted to water
exercises.exp: Magnetic force passes through water and most non-magnetic materials — the magnet can pick up clips through the glass!

exercises.question: What does it mean to say a material is MAGNETIC?
choices: it can be attracted to a magnet
exercises.exp: A magnetic material is one that is attracted to a magnet — mainly iron, steel, nickel, and cobalt.

exercises.question: You have a bar magnet. You break it in half. Now you have ___.
choices: one N piece and one S piece (only one pole each)
two complete magnets, each with its own N and S poles
two pieces with no magnetic properties
one stronger magnet and one weak one
exercises.exp: Every piece of a magnet is a complete magnet! Each half has both N and S poles — you can never separate the poles.

exercises.question: Magnetic force is a ___.
choices: contact force — magnets must touch to attract
non-contact force — magnets attract and repel without touching
exercises.exp: Magnets attract or repel at a distance — they do not need to touch! That makes magnetism a non-contact force.

exercises.question: Which type of metal is MOST magnetic?
exercises.exp: Iron is the most commonly magnetic metal. It is strongly attracted to magnets and can become magnetised itself.

exercises.question: A crane at a scrapyard uses a GIANT ELECTROMAGNET to pick up old cars. What happens when the electricity is turned OFF?
choices: the cars are held even more tightly
the electromagnet stops working and the cars fall
exercises.exp: An electromagnet only works when electricity flows through it. Turn off the current — magnetic force stops — cars drop!

exercises.question: The N pole of a magnet faces another N pole. They ___.
exercises.exp: Same poles (N and N) repel — they push each other away. Like poles always repel!

exercises.question: Which everyday tool uses a MAGNET to hold things together?
choices: a magnetic clasp on a bag or necklace
exercises.exp: Many bags, jewellery clasps, and cabinet doors use magnets to snap together — convenient and strong!

exercises.question: Iron filings are sprinkled around a bar magnet. They form a pattern showing ___.
choices: the magnetic field lines around the magnet — strongest at the poles
exercises.exp: Iron filings align with magnetic field lines — forming a beautiful pattern that shows the invisible magnetic field!

exercises.question: If you hang a bar magnet by a string, it will spin until ___.
choices: its North pole points toward geographic North
exercises.exp: A freely hanging magnet acts like a compass — it aligns with Earth's magnetic field, with N pointing North!

exercises.question: Scientists use MRI machines to scan the human body. MRI stands for Magnetic Resonance Imaging. These machines use ___.
exercises.exp: MRI machines use incredibly powerful magnets to create detailed images of the inside of your body — medicine and magnets!

exercises.question: Which test would you use to find out if an unknown metal is MAGNETIC?
choices: test it with a magnet and see if it is attracted
exercises.exp: The simplest test: hold a magnet near the metal. If it is attracted, the metal is magnetic — easy science experiment!

exercises.question: A magnet has TWO poles. They are called ___.
exercises.exp: Every magnet has a North pole and a South pole — and the magnetic force is strongest at both poles!

exercises.question: Opposite poles ___.
choices: have no effect on each other
exercises.exp: Opposite poles (N and S) attract — they pull toward each other! Same poles (N-N or S-S) repel.

exercises.question: Same poles ___.
exercises.exp: Same poles repel — N pushes away N, S pushes away S. Try pushing two north poles together — they push apart!

exercises.question: Which material is attracted to a magnet?
exercises.exp: Iron is magnetic — it is attracted to magnets. Plastic, wood, and glass are not magnetic materials.

exercises.question: Can magnets attract through materials like paper or your hand?
choices: yes — magnetic force can pass through many non-magnetic materials
exercises.exp: Yes! Magnetic force can pass through paper, plastic, wood, water, and even your hand — it is amazing! (Weaker through thick materials.)

exercises.question: A compass needle points NORTH because ___.
choices: north is where the sun rises
Earth itself acts like a giant magnet
the needle is powered by a battery
exercises.exp: Earth has a magnetic field like a giant bar magnet. A compass needle aligns with this field, pointing to magnetic North.

exercises.question: Which of these is NOT magnetic?
exercises.exp: Aluminium is NOT magnetic — even though it is a metal. Only iron, nickel, cobalt, and their alloys are magnetic!

exercises.question: What do we call the region around a magnet where its force acts?
exercises.exp: The magnetic field is the invisible region around a magnet where magnetic forces act on other magnetic materials.

exercises.question: If you CUT a bar magnet in half, you get ___.
choices: one N pole and one S pole separately
two smaller magnets, each with its own N and S poles
two pieces that are no longer magnetic
exercises.exp: Cut a magnet and each piece becomes its own complete magnet with both a N and S pole — magnets cannot be split into separate poles!

exercises.question: Which of these uses MAGNETISM to work?
exercises.exp: A compass uses Earth's magnetic field — its magnetic needle aligns with Earth's poles to show direction.

exercises.question: Maglev trains float above the track using ___.
choices: magnetic repulsion — magnets on the train and track push each other
exercises.exp: Maglev (magnetic levitation) trains use powerful magnets that repel each other — the train literally floats above the track!

exercises.question: A horseshoe magnet is strong because ___.
choices: both poles are close together, doubling the magnetic force in one area
the curved shape makes it faster
exercises.exp: Both poles of a horseshoe magnet face the same direction — their combined force picks up much heavier objects than a bar magnet!

exercises.question: Which item would a magnet PICK UP from a pile of mixed objects?
exercises.exp: Steel contains iron — magnetic! Plastic, copper, and rubber are not magnetic so the magnet would ignore them.

exercises.question: Magnetic force gets ___.
choices: stronger as you move farther away
weaker as you move farther away
exercises.exp: Magnetic force decreases with distance — the farther away from the magnet, the weaker the force. Close = strong!

exercises.question: You can make a TEMPORARY magnet by ___.
choices: repeatedly stroking an iron nail with one end of a magnet in the same direction
dipping an iron nail in water
exercises.exp: Stroking iron with a magnet aligns its magnetic domains, making it temporarily magnetic. This is called induced magnetism!

exercises.question: A fridge magnet sticks to the fridge door because the door is made of ___.
exercises.exp: Fridge doors are typically made of steel — which contains iron. Iron is attracted to magnets, so the magnet sticks!

exercises.question: Which of these everyday objects contains a MAGNET inside?
exercises.exp: Electric doorbells use an electromagnet that vibrates a clapper to make the ringing sound — magnets inside!

exercises.question: An ELECTROMAGNET is different from a permanent magnet because ___.
choices: it can be turned on and off by controlling electric current
it only works at low temperatures
exercises.exp: Electromagnets are created by electric current through wire. Turn the current off and the magnetism stops — super useful!

exercises.question: You want to separate magnetic metals from a recycling bin of mixed materials. The best tool is ___.
choices: a large electromagnet to pick up magnetic metals only
exercises.exp: Recycling plants use large electromagnets to pull magnetic metals (steel cans) out of mixed recycling — efficient and clever!

exercises.question: Both a bar magnet and Earth act like magnets. What do they have in common?
choices: both are made of solid iron
both have North and South poles and create a magnetic field
exercises.exp: Both have N and S poles and create magnetic fields around them. Earth's field even protects us from solar radiation!
